trace.topic: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More.
trace.goal: Explain the paradox that AI agents increase managerial and operational work.
expected_facts: The answer should explain that AI agents expand what teams can attempt, which often increases work.
It should argue that management, supervision, and orchestration become more important, not less.
It should connect the paradox to founder expectations about leverage.
rubric_must_haves: Names and explains the paradox clearly.
Connects the idea to day-to-day operating reality.
Includes a concrete implication for founders or managers.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should explain that AI agents create leverage, but leverage usually expands the amount of work teams attempt rather than shrinking the need for judgment and management. As a result, founders often find themselves supervising more workflows, more experiments, and more exceptions. The lesson is to expect amplified operations, not effortless simplification.

trace.answer: We all thought we’d use AI Agents to do less work. To let us off the hook on some tasks, if not all of them. That sounds nice. But what actually happened? The opposite. We’re working harder than ever. Here’s what I mean. For decades, there was this simple math: hire someone, pay $X per year + benefits, get Y units of output. Simple. Easy. Predictable. Then came SaaS. Suddenly software could automate tons of stuff—support tickets, marketing automation, workflows—and the cost equation changed dramatically. Now you could get Z units of output for maybe half the price of an employee. Plus no overhead, no benefits, no drama. So everyone started automating everything. And then … nothing. Because they didn’t change how much work they did. They just gave the remaining work to fewer people. Which meant those people worked harder. And burned out faster. And quit. Or stayed miserable. Same problem, different container. That’s the Cowan paradox. We thought AI would free us up. Instead, it made us complicit in our own exhaustion.
trace.raw_model_output: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More. What if the productivity gains from AI weren’t actually productivity gains? What if instead of freeing us up to focus on high-value tasks, we’re using AI to do MORE stuff at the same intensity level? Here’s what I’ve learned after living this reality for two years. 🤖 The 24/7 Pace Trap The real problem isn’t that AI makes us busier — although it certainly does. It’s that AI agents operate without boundaries. No weekends. No vacations. No “I’m exhausted” responses. When your team member quits on Friday afternoon and never comes back, there’s no notice period. There’s no conversation. There’s just silence. Your remaining team picks up the slack. Now imagine those same team members working alongside AI agents that never rest. Never complain. Never say no. The cognitive load compounds. Every alert. Every notification. Every decision point where you consider whether to let the agent handle something versus taking it yourself. The mental overhead becomes exhausting. And it doesn’t feel like exhaustion. It feels like productivity. Because you ARE being productive. You’re handling twice the volume you could have handled six months ago. You’re shipping faster. You’re responding immediately. You’re crushing targets. But deep down, you know you’re running on empty. 🚀 The Acceleration Feedback Loop What happens next is predictable but devastating. You accelerate further because you can. You push harder because the tools allow it. You optimize processes until they break

retrieval_hits.text: Because AI, used right, enables you to do more things at scale than were ever possible before.

"20 AI Agents aren't less work than the humans they replaced.

But it's just ... easier.  They don't quit, they don't stop, they don't need promotions or even career growth.

It's easier to work with well-trained AI Agents than ... mid-pack and below humans."  More below

This is why AI will soon take 50%+ of sales jobs

Not because we don’t need sales.  But because AI can do a better job than this.

2. The Always-On Pressure
Humans naturally create boundaries. We go home, we sleep, we disconnect. AI agents don’t. This creates an insidious pressure to match their pace.
I caught myself checking AI-generated reports at 11 PM because “the agents found something important.” This isn’t sustainable, and it’s not what AI was supposed to solve.
